question: What is the cell membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber called?
explanation: The sarcolemma acts as the outer skin or cell membrane for individual muscle fibers, helping conduct electrical signals. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h1)

question: How are the thick and thin protein filaments arranged inside a sarcomere?

options.A: Thick filaments anchor the Z-lines while thin filaments stay in the center
options.B: Thin filaments occupy the center while thick filaments form the outer borders
options.C: Thick filaments float freely in the sarcoplasm without protein attachments
options.D: Thin filaments anchor to Z-lines and extend toward the center of the sarcomere

explanation: Thin actin filaments attach directly to the Z-lines at either end and reach inward to overlap with thick myosin filaments. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which regulatory protein does calcium bind to when a muscle is stimulated to contract?
explanation: Calcium ions bind directly to troponin, causing a physical shift that moves tropomyosin out of the way. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h2)

question: What happens immediately after calcium ions bind to troponin on the thin filament?

options.A: The Z-lines dissolve completely to shorten the myofibril
options.B: Tropomyosin shifts position to expose actin binding sites
options.C: ATP is synthesized rapidly inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.D: Myosin heads detach permanently from the thick filament

explanation: Moving troponin pulls tropomyosin aside, clearing the path for myosin heads to attach to actin. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the name of the theory that explains how muscle fibers shorten during contraction?
explanation: The sliding filament theory explains how thin actin filaments slide past thick myosin filaments to shorten the muscle unit. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h3)

question: What happens to the actual length of the protein filaments when a muscle contracts?

options.A: Thin filaments lengthen while thick filaments shorten
options.B: The filaments stay the same length while sliding past each other
options.C: Both thick and thin filaments shorten in length
options.D: Thick filaments stretch out while thin filaments dissolve

explanation: Contraction happens because filaments slide past one another, not because the individual protein molecules shrink or stretch. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h3)

question: What molecule must bind to the myosin head so it can release its hold on actin?
explanation: A fresh ATP molecule is required for the myosin head to let go of the actin filament. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h4)

question: What does the myosin head do right after forming a cross-bridge with actin?

options.A: It pumps calcium back into storage vesicles
options.B: It pivots to pull the actin filament inward
options.C: It dissolves into the surrounding sarcoplasm
options.D: It manufactures extra molecules of glucose

explanation: The power stroke involves the myosin head pivoting, which slides the actin filament toward the center. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h4)

question: Where are calcium ions stored when a skeletal muscle is resting?
explanation: Calcium is safely stored inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum until a nerve signal prompts its release. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why do muscles stiffen in rigor mortis after death when ATP is gone?

options.A: Tropomyosin permanently blocks all actin sites without exception
options.B: Actin and myosin filaments disintegrate completely into free amino acids
options.C: Excess ATP causes muscles to contract without stopping until exhaustion
options.D: Calcium cannot be pumped away, so cross-bridges remain permanently locked

explanation: Without ATP to detach myosin from actin, muscles stay stuck in a contracted state after death. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h5)

question: A woman in labor receives oxytocin to help her uterus contract. How does oxytocin help this process?

options.A: By replacing ATP with alternative fuel sources in muscle cells
options.B: By blocking troponin so actin can never bind to myosin heads
options.C: By increasing intracellular calcium availability in uterine muscle
options.D: By dissolving the Z-lines of the myometrium to speed up delivery

explanation: Oxytocin stimulates uterine smooth muscle by promoting calcium entry, which triggers stronger muscle contractions. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is linked directly to painful muscle cramps and spasms?
explanation: Low calcium makes nerve and muscle cell membranes unstable, causing them to fire spontaneously and trigger painful cramps. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T5#BMP111_U3_T5_h6)
